1 summary: FixSaathi is a real-time AI repair copilot, built on Gemini Live, that sees through a field technician's phone camera and talks them through diagnosing and fixing ACs, home appliances and rooftop-solar equipment, hands-free and in Hindi or English, so the job gets done right on the first visit and the service report writes itself.
2 problem: India is buying ACs, appliances and rooftop solar much faster than it can train people to repair them. Room AC sales hit a record 12.5-13 million units in FY2025 (ICRA), over 50 lakh homes have added rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar, and CEEW estimates India will need about 2 million skilled AC technicians by 2036-37, up from 0.37 million in 2022-23. Most technicians today learned on the job; only about one in four informal AC technicians has any formal training (CEEW). So when a fault is unfamiliar, they guess, call a senior or search YouTube. That leads to wrong diagnoses, wasted parts and repeat visits: the service company loses money, the technician loses a day's earnings and the customer keeps waiting. Training alone can't close this gap quickly; technicians need expert help right there on the job. Jitendra, an AC and appliance technician in Mumbai, told us that in old homes reversed wiring can keep a line live even after the switch is off, a danger a beginner can easily miss.
3 user:
Our user is the field technician: usually 20 to 40 years old, fixing ACs, fridges, washing machines, fans, inverters or rooftop-solar systems. They often work alone at a customer's home, carry a mid-range Android phone, prefer speaking Hindi or their regional language to typing, get paid per job, and rarely have a senior nearby when they hit a fault they haven't seen before.
Our paying customers are the businesses that employ these technicians and pay for every repeat visit: authorised service centres of AC, appliance and solar brands, multi-brand repair companies, home-services platforms, rooftop-solar installers, and facility-management firms looking after offices, hospitals and housing societies. Their managers want more first-time fixes, faster onboarding of new technicians and clean digital service reports.
Independent technicians are our third group. A low-cost personal plan helps them take on jobs they would otherwise turn down.
4 solution:
FixSaathi puts an experienced senior in the technician's pocket. A repair works like this:
1. See: the technician points the camera at the machine, and Gemini recognises the appliance, brand and model, reading specs off the label.
2. Listen: they describe the problem by voice in Hindi or English, and the AI asks quick follow-up questions.
3. Safety first: no repair steps unlock until the AI confirms the power is off and other precautions are done.
4. Diagnose: it ranks the likely faults and marks the suspect part on screen.
5. Guide: it talks them through the fix one step at a time, checks each step on camera and calls in a senior if it is unsure.
6. Report: it writes the service report automatically, with the fault, parts used and before/after photos, for the manager's dashboard.
Every repair adds to a shared fault knowledge base, so the guidance gets better over time. It runs on mid-range Android phones and understands Hinglish.

6 business:
We will sell FixSaathi as B2B SaaS, priced per technician per month.
1. Service centres and repair companies (our core customers): about Rs 299-499 per technician for live guidance, automatic service reports and a manager dashboard. Saving even one or two repeat visits a month pays for it.
2. Brands (AC, appliance, solar): enterprise plans with brand-specific repair guides, a private fault knowledge base and analytics on which parts fail by model and region, to cut warranty costs.
3. Independent technicians: freemium, with a few free guided repairs each month and a small fee after that, which drives bottom-up adoption.
Extra revenue: commission on genuine spare parts ordered in the app, and paid skill certifications.
Go-to-market: pilots with multi-brand service centres and rooftop-solar installers in Bengaluru, who feel repeat-visit costs directly. Then we scale through home-services platforms and brand service networks, where one partnership can bring in hundreds of technicians.
7 competitors:
A stuck technician has four options today, and none really solves the problem:
1. YouTube videos and service manuals: free, but generic, rarely about the exact machine, not hands-free and mostly in English.
2. Remote-expert video tools like TeamViewer Frontline: connect the technician to a human expert, but a paid expert must sit on every call, which is costly and hard to scale.
3. Field-service software like Salesforce Field Service, Zoho FSM and Fieldproxy: good for scheduling and tracking, but they don't help fix the fault.
4. Calling a senior: helpful, but seniors are few, busy at peak times and can't see the machine.
FixSaathi is an AI expert that sees the machine live, speaks the technician's language, guides them hands-free with safety checks built in and writes the report on its own, at a fraction of the cost of a human expert. It also plugs into existing service software. Our moat is data: every repair adds verified fault-to-fix data by brand, model and region that is hard to copy.
8 countries:
Primary market: India. It is a huge and fast-growing service market, with a record 12.5-13 million room ACs sold in FY2025, over 50 lakh rooftop-solar installations under PM Surya Ghar, rising fridge and washing-machine ownership, and a workforce that is mostly trained on the job. We will start in Bengaluru, then expand to Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Hyderabad and Pune, and add regional languages like Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi and Bengali to reach tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
Secondary markets: Southeast and South Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Bangladesh), where appliance ownership is climbing fast and technicians face the same training gap and language needs; and the Middle East (UAE and Saudi Arabia), where ACs run almost all year and much of the technician workforce already speaks Hindi or Urdu.
FixSaathi does not depend on a single language or appliance, so entering a new country mostly means adding local languages and brand data, not rebuilding the product.
9 ai:
AI is the product itself, not a feature added on top. We use it for:
1. Live vision: recognising the appliance, model, parts and visible faults like burns, leaks or loose wires.
2. Voice: hands-free conversation in Hindi and English, with more Indian languages next.
3. Diagnosis: combining what it sees with what the technician says to rank likely causes and pick the next check.
4. Safety and step checks: confirming each step on camera and blocking risky actions until precautions are done.
5. Part location: Gemini finds the faulty part and the app marks it on screen.
6. Reports: turning each session into a structured service report.
7. Offline help: an on-device safety checklist and job notes that sync later.
8. Learning: anonymised repair outcomes keep improving future diagnoses.
We tested this on photos of our own appliances: Gemini read brands and specs off the labels, spotted loose fan wiring and a damp, cracked ceiling on its own, and gave safety-first steps in Hinglish.
10 models:
Gemini Live is the heart of the experience. It streams the technician's camera and voice in real time, understands the machine and the problem described in Hindi or English, and answers with spoken step-by-step guidance, so they never have to type or look away from the repair. They can interrupt it, just like a senior.
Gemini API powers our reasoning agents. A diagnosis agent ranks likely faults and chooses the next check, a safety agent blocks risky steps until precautions are confirmed, and a report agent turns each session into a structured JSON service report. Function calling links them to the fault knowledge base, spare-part lookup and brand manuals.
Nano Banana creates visual step cards for complex repairs. To mark the faulty part, Gemini returns its exact position and our app draws the marker, so it is always accurate.
Gemma runs on the phone for weak-network sites. It handles the safety checklist and saves job notes and photos offline, then syncs once the phone is back online.
11 deploy:
Our backend runs as containers on Cloud Run in asia-south1 (Mumbai). It scales from zero to thousands of live repair sessions on its own, so we only pay for what we use. A session service on Cloud Run securely relays live audio and video to Gemini Live, with Vertex AI handling production model access, quotas and monitoring.
Firestore stores technicians, jobs, reports and the fault knowledge base in real time, with each service company's data kept separate. Firebase Authentication handles sign-in and Firebase Hosting serves the manager dashboard. Cloud Storage keeps repair photos, Pub/Sub sends finished reports to dashboards and partner systems, and BigQuery powers anonymised fault analytics for brands. Secret Manager protects our keys, Cloud Build ships every update, and Cloud Logging and Monitoring track speed and errors.
To scale, we add Google Cloud regions as we enter new countries and use Agent Skills to add new appliance types without redesigning the system.
